system.name: Fisslock
system.one_liner: an in-network lock management system that scales using a technique called lock fission

components.name: Match-Action Unit (MAU)
components.role: one pipeline stage that matches packet header fields against tables and executes the selected action; shown exploded here and recurring in both the ingress and egress pipelines

components.name: ALUs
components.role: arithmetic-logic units that execute the action selected by a match

components.name: Match-Action Tables
components.role: map header field values to actions; split into stateless and stateful tables

components.name: Register Arrays
components.role: per-stage stateful memory that is read and updated by the ALUs

components.name: Packet Headers
components.role: input header fields entering the pipeline

components.name: Modified Packet Headers
components.role: output header fields leaving the pipeline

components.name: Programmable Switch (PS)
components.role: the switch that hosts the control-plane CPU/DRAM and the data-plane packet-processing pipeline

components.name: CPU
components.role: runs the Linux-based control-plane operating system

components.name: DRAM
components.role: memory attached to the control-plane CPU

components.name: Parser
components.role: extracts packet header fields for the ingress pipeline

components.name: Traffic Mgr.
components.role: switches packets between the ingress and egress pipelines, replicating for multicast

components.name: Deparser
components.role: reassembles header fields after the egress pipeline

components.name: Ingress Ports
components.role: physical ports where packets enter the switch

components.name: Egress Ports
components.role: physical ports where packets leave the switch, possibly replicated

content.key_idea: A programmable switch splits into a CPU/DRAM control plane and an ASIC data plane whose match-action-unit pipeline stages hold register arrays that ALUs read and update under table-selected actions.

summary: This figure supplies background on the programmable-switch hardware that Fisslock, an in-network lock-fission system, later builds on. The right-hand Programmable Switch (PS) box stacks a control plane, a general-purpose CPU with DRAM running Linux, above a data-plane pipeline: incoming packet headers pass through a Parser into ingress Match-Action Units, are steered by a Traffic Mgr. that can replicate packets for multicast, continue through egress Match-Action Units, and leave through a Deparser as modified packet headers. The left-hand panel explodes a single Match-Action Unit (MAU) to show its internals: ALUs execute actions chosen from stateless and stateful Match-Action Tables, which read and update per-stage Register Arrays. No lock-specific components appear; the figure only establishes switch pipeline stages and per-MAU memory limits.

notes: layout-proposal: exploded-stage-beside-pipeline — a single Match-Action Unit's internals (ALUs, tables, register arrays) are exploded on the left, wired via a shared Packet-Headers arrow into the right panel's full switch pipeline (control-plane CPU/DRAM over a parser-MAU-traffic-manager-MAU-deparser data plane), where that same stage recurs twice.
